messages.subject: replicate bayesian piecewise linear mixed models with a random change point
parts:
Hi folks,

I want to replicate Bayesian piecewise linear mixed models with a random change point in this paper: https://github.com/sambrilleman/2017-Epidemiology/blob/master/all_stan_models/SimStudy_stan_randomknotcorr.stan. From my perspective, I believe my nimble code is functioning correctly. However, the results are unable to capture the true value. Could you please help me review my code first?

Please find the attached file containing my simulated function and nimble code.

Thank you, 
Hao

messages.author: c242febbf5e3a49a
messages.subject: Re: replicate bayesian piecewise linear mixed models with a random change point
parts:
Here is the updated nimble code. I believe the code is correct this time. In case anyone is interested in this model, I have attached it below.

mod <- nimbleCode({
  # Priors
  beta[1] ~ dnorm(20, 1/20^2)
  beta[2] ~ dnorm(0, 1/4^2)
  beta[3] ~ dnorm(0, 1/4^2)
  betakp ~ dunif(betakp_lower, betakp_upper)
 
  for (i in 1:4) {
    u_sd[i] ~ dt(0, 1/5, 1) # T-distribution with 1 degree of freedom
  }
 
  y_sd ~ dt(0.001, 1/5, 1) # T-distribution with 1 degree of freedom and a small positive location parameter
 
  # Correlation matrix
  L_u_Corr[1:4,1:4] ~ dlkj_corr_cholesky(1, 4) # LKJ prior on the Cholesky factor of the correlation matrix
 
  # Random effects
  for (i in 1:Npat) {
    uRaw[i,1:4] ~ dmnorm(mu[1:4], L_u_Corr[1:4,1:4])
    for (j in 1:4) {
      u[i,j] <- u_sd[j] * uRaw[i,j]
    }
    for (k in 1:3) {
      alpha[i,k] <- beta[k] + u[i,k]
    }
    alpha[i,4] <- betakp + u[i,4]
  }
 
  # Regression equation
  for (j in 1:N) {
    indicator[j] <- step(alpha[id[j],4] - age[j]) # 1 if age[j] < alpha[id[j],4], 0 otherwise
    y_mu[j] <- alpha[id[j],1] + (alpha[id[j],2] * indicator[j] + alpha[id[j],3] * (1 - indicator[j])) * (age[j] - alpha[id[j],4])
  }
 
  # Likelihood
  for (i in 1:N) {
    y[i] ~ dnorm(y_mu[i], 1/y_sd^2)
  }
} )
